architecture.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: updated architecture PNG for three AWS Amplify support-ticket repositories.
Input image: the supplied old architecture diagram is a style and content reference. Replace its obsolete manual WebSocket lookup lane and historical local-only status with the current implementation. Re-layout substantially where needed for legibility; preserve the crisp professional style, AWS-style flat service icons, white canvas, dark navy typography, pale green/lavender/amber/blue group panels, aligned boxes, and clean orthogonal arrows. High-resolution wide landscape, approximately 16:9. Large readable text, generous whitespace.

Title exactly: "SupportDesk: Live Ticket Updates".
Subtitle exactly: "REST + GraphQL writes → DynamoDB Streams → WebSocket push".

Show these technically correct flows, with unambiguous arrowheads and minimal crossings:
1. Top identity strip: "Ticket owner / Agent" → "Amazon Cognito" → "ID token"; a small caption says the browser carries this token to APIs. Never draw Cognito directly invoking REST or AppSync.
2. REST write/read lane: "Browser" → "API Gateway REST" → authorizer branches → "ticketRest" Lambda → the ONE shared "Ticket table". The branches read "Cognito authorizer" with "/tickets · /tickets/{id} · comments", and "Lambda authorizer" with "/admin/tickets · Agents only".
3. GraphQL lane: Browser → "AWS AppSync" (subtitle "Cognito authorization") → two branches. "Generated CRUD resolvers" directly connects to the same Ticket table, bypassing Lambda. "ticketWorkflow" Lambda, subtitle "Summary · close · comments", connects to that same Ticket table.
4. Main new highlighted event-flow lane, reading right-to-left if that avoids crossings: the same Ticket table → "DynamoDB Streams" (subtitle "NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES") → "ticketSocketHandler" Lambda (subtitle "Filter owner / Agents · check expiry") → "API Gateway WebSocket" → Browser. Bold green arrows labeled "Automatic push". This must be a SERVER-TO-BROWSER push flow. The websocket gateway is used as a return transport here, not as a request to query tickets.
5. A dashed separate connect/control flow from Browser to API Gateway WebSocket labeled "Authenticated connection". A callout beside the gateway reads "At $connect: Lambda verifies Cognito token". Keep this distinct from the notification data path. The same reusable authorizer verifies both the Agents REST route and WebSocket connect.
6. "Connections table" is a separate small DynamoDB cylinder attached to ticketSocketHandler with a thin read/manage connection link. Caption: "Connection ID · owner · groups · JWT expiry · TTL". Its contents are connection records, NOT tickets. The broadcaster scans authorized live connections, removes expired/gone connections, and posts to their callback endpoints. No extra standalone broadcaster Lambda: ticketSocketHandler is reused.
7. The Ticket table caption says "Tickets + stored comments". All REST, generated GraphQL, and workflow Lambda writes converge on this one Ticket table WITHIN EACH PROJECT. No separate comments table.
8. Short note in the push lane: "New ticket · status/title change · new comment". Another short note: "Push metadata; load comment text through the protected API". Do not imply comment bodies are broadcast.
9. A concise bottom workflow strip says "Create ticket / change status / add comment → other authorized browsers update automatically". A small note says "Pause / resume · reconnect + resync".
10. Footer has three separated project cards: "Gen 1" with "Categories + overrides + custom CDK"; "Native Gen 2" with "TypeScript + CDK"; "Migrated Gen 2" with "Repaired independent backend". Footer text exactly: "Separate pools, APIs, Ticket tables, and Connections tables per project". Small status: "Deployed and verified · 7 October 2026".

Omit the old "Read via WebSocket" lookup strip, getTicket lookup emphasis, and "Local validation only" banner. Do not add Figma, Amplify Studio, frontend hosting, queues, pub/sub services, or resource sharing between the three projects. Prefer short labels, fewer bigger boxes, complete arrow paths, and accurate semantics to dense prose. No photos, 3D, watermark, decorative scenery, or tiny unreadable labels.

sequence.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: companion sequence diagram PNG for repository documentation.
Input image: use the supplied NEW architecture image ONLY as a style reference. Create a new sequence diagram, not another architecture diagram. Match its white background, navy headings, pale green/lavender/amber/blue bands, flat AWS-style icons and clean readable typography. Wide high-resolution landscape, approximately 16:9, large crisp labels, generous margins.

Title exactly: "How Live Updates Reach Another Browser".
Subtitle exactly: "Status changes and comments appear without manual refresh".

Use six evenly spaced participant columns left to right, thin vertical lifelines and clear horizontal directed arrows:
"Browser A"
"REST API"
"Ticket table + Streams"
"ticketSocketHandler"
"WebSocket Gateway"
"Browser B"
The REST API column may have the subtitle "ticketRest Lambda". Browser B subtitle exactly "Owner / Agent · ticket selected".
At the top, a separate authentication banner says "Both browsers sign in with Cognito and open an authenticated WebSocket connection". Small note: "$connect Lambda verifies the Cognito ID token".

Two shaded groups in chronological downward order:
GROUP 1 heading "Change ticket status", pale green:
1. Browser A → REST API: "PATCH /tickets/{id} · IN_PROGRESS".
2. REST API → Ticket table + Streams: "Persist status".
3. Ticket table + Streams → ticketSocketHandler: "DynamoDB stream event".
4. A compact self-check note by ticketSocketHandler: "Owner / Agents check + JWT expiry".
5. ticketSocketHandler → WebSocket Gateway: "Push ticketChanged metadata".
6. WebSocket Gateway → Browser B: "Update queue + selected status".
Make all six numbered steps easy to follow and avoid reversed arrows.

GROUP 2 heading "Add a ticket comment", pale lavender:
7. Browser A → REST API: "POST /tickets/{id}/comments".
8. REST API → Ticket table + Streams: "Append comment + verified author".
9. Ticket table + Streams → ticketSocketHandler: "Stream commentAdded".
10. ticketSocketHandler → WebSocket Gateway: "Push commentsChanged=true".
11. WebSocket Gateway → Browser B: "New-comment notification".
12. Browser B → REST API: "GET /tickets/{id}/comments".
13. REST API → Browser B: "Return stored comments".
The last two arrows traverse right-to-left and left-to-right respectively; show clear arrowheads on distinct horizontal rows so their destinations are unambiguous. These HTTP comment reads are protected by Cognito and ticket owner/Agents access. Browser B already has the ticket selected, which is why it loads its comments. Comment bodies are NOT included in the WebSocket push.

Bottom notes in readable compact cards:
"WebSocket pushes metadata; comment text comes from the protected API".
"Pause / resume: reconnect and resync current state".
"Generated GraphQL writes and custom Lambda status changes use the same stream-to-push path".
Footer: "Gen 1 · Native Gen 2 · Migrated Gen 2 — separate resources, same behavior".
Small date: "Verified · 7 October 2026".

Do not include a manual WebSocket getTicket/lookup step. Do not use polling, AppSync subscriptions, extra broadcaster functions, queues, or resource sharing. Avoid tangled diagonal arrows, tiny fonts, dense paragraphs, invalid AWS routing, screenshots, photos, gradients obscuring text, 3D, or watermarks. Preserve technical accuracy rather than decorative detail.

verification: REST and GraphQL converge on the same Ticket table within each project
Generated CRUD bypasses the workflow Lambda
DynamoDB Streams invokes the existing socket handler
Socket handler filters owner/Agents and JWT expiry
WebSocket pushes metadata; protected API returns comment text
Connections table is separate from Ticket storage
Visual arrow/text inspection completed for both images
